h1:
Rayong Breakfast
The Way Locals Eat It
intro: People in Rayong wake up early and take breakfast seriously. The fresh market is busy before sunrise, noodle and congee pots are boiling by six, and the old-town cafes open later in the morning. This is the breakfast locals actually eat — from hot bowls in the market to coffee along Yomjinda Road.

blocks.html: Rayong is a better breakfast town than you might expect. In the city center you'll find morning markets that open before dawn, decades-old noodle shops, hot congee and pork blood soup, and the old-town stretch of Yomjinda Road that has turned into a cafe district. We've picked out savory dishes, sweets and places to sit with a coffee, with straight talk on neighborhoods and opening hours. We haven't eaten at every shop ourselves — most of this leans on what locals say in reviews, so double-check the hours before you head out.

If you want to see how Rayong locals really do breakfast, start at a market. The food is fresh, the prices are easy on the wallet, and you get to watch everyday city life along the way. These two are the main morning markets in town.

items.name: Wat Lum Market (morning)
items.blurb: A downtown morning market that opens before dawn, roughly 04:30–09:30. You'll find rice-and-curry plates, fried snacks, Thai sweets, fruit and dishes to take home. Good for buying food in the early hours and finding a spot to eat nearby.

items.name: Star Fresh Market
items.blurb: A large fresh market in the city center with raw ingredients, ready-made dishes and several morning food stalls to choose from. This is where Rayong locals regularly stop to buy dishes to bring home.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The good stuff at morning markets tends to sell out fast. If you want hot fried snacks or a popular Thai sweet, get there before seven and you'll have far more to choose from.

blocks.text: Noodles, Kuay Jub, Congee & Pork Blood Soup

blocks.html: This is the star of breakfast in Rayong. Noodle and congee shops run from early morning into midday, and many have been around long enough to be local landmarks. We've ordered them by popularity and how long they've been open, not by a fixed ranking of which tastes best — everyone has different preferences.

items.name: Kuay Jub Tong Je (Pa Malee)
items.blurb: Old-style thick-broth kuay jub that's been selling for over 36 years. The standout is the crispy pork fried fresh each day, a rich, aromatic five-spice broth, and fried wontons you can add. Locals bring this one up often when they think of kuay jub.

items.name: Sapha Jok
items.blurb: A full-spread breakfast spot in town with smooth pork congee, boiled and fried chicken rice, clear-broth pork noodles, pork blood soup and soft-rib soup. Great if you come as a group and want to order a bit of everything.

items.name: Jok Nai Jua
items.blurb: A congee shop locals praise for thick, finely-ground congee loaded with toppings. Good for anyone who likes it smooth rather than grainy — an easy, light breakfast before heading out for the day.

items.name: Wilaiwan Pork Blood Rice (Saphan Piam)
items.blurb: Opens very early, around 05:30, with pork blood soup plus boiled and fried chicken rice. This is the shop for early risers who want something hot to fuel up before the day starts.

items.name: Cha Kang Rao
items.blurb: A breakfast spot that opens at six, with noodles, chicken rice, pork blood soup and single-plate dishes. Good if you want somewhere open early with a varied menu all in one place.

items.name: Kuay Jub Yai Mee (by Wat Khot Hin)
items.blurb: An old-school kuay jub spot that's been selling for over 20 years, in a lane beside Wat Khot Hin. Open from morning to afternoon, it's a regular for the Khao Phai crowd who like traditional clear-broth kuay jub.

items.name: Kin Phuea Yu Breakfast
items.blurb: A relaxed breakfast spot where people talk about the pork blood soup and the mild pork-seaweed-glass-noodle soup. Not too strong on flavor — good if you want to start the day with something light and brothy.

blocks.html: Dim sum is another favorite Rayong breakfast — order several baskets to share over hot tea, prices are easy, and most of it follows southern Thai / Hat Yai recipes made fresh each day.

items: 100 Lan Dim Sum — southern-style dim sum with over 30 kinds to choose from, made fresh daily, from about ฿20 per basket
Hat Yai-style dim sum in town — pork dumplings, shrimp har gow, steamed buns, and specials like bak kut teh, around ฿25 per basket; great for ordering a spread to share
How to order dim sum — order just a few baskets at a time and top up as you go, so everything stays hot and fresh through the meal

blocks.text: Morning Coffee in the Yomjinda Old Town

blocks.html: After the savory food, people like to follow up with coffee around Yomjinda Road — Rayong's old town, where century-old Sino-Portuguese shophouses have been renovated into cafes. Most open later, around nine, making them a good rest stop once you've finished the morning market.

items.name: Old House At Yomjinda
items.blurb: A two-story wooden-house cafe done up in vintage style on Yomjinda Road, with plenty of photo corners and an old-days feel. Good for a long, slow coffee after walking the old town. Open roughly 09:00–18:00.

items.name: Yajindom
items.blurb: A homey Thai-dessert cafe on Yomjinda Road serving Thai sweets alongside modern-style drinks. Great if you like something sweet with your coffee. Open roughly 10:00–17:00, closed Wednesday.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Cafes around Yomjinda open late. If you're up early, eat your savory breakfast at the market first, then wander into the old town for coffee later in the morning — the timing works out just right.

faq.q: What do Rayong locals eat for breakfast?
faq.a: Popular savory choices are noodles, thick-broth kuay jub, congee, pork blood soup and chicken rice. People who prefer a set spread tend to go for dim sum, then follow up with coffee in the Yomjinda old town.

faq.q: What time do Rayong's morning markets open?
faq.a: Wat Lum Market in the morning opens around 04:30–09:30 and is a before-dawn market in the city center. Star Fresh Market is a large fresh market with plenty of morning food stalls. Aim to get there before seven for the full selection.

faq.q: Where should I go for morning kuay jub in Rayong?
faq.a: The one locals mention most is Kuay Jub Tong Je (Pa Malee), thick-broth kuay jub with crispy pork that's been selling for over 36 years, open around 08:00–17:00 and closed Sunday. Another is Kuay Jub Yai Mee beside Wat Khot Hin, open from morning to afternoon.

faq.q: Which area has good morning coffee in Rayong?
faq.a: Yomjinda Road in the old town is the main cafe district, with spots like Old House At Yomjinda and Yajindom. Most open later, around nine or ten, so they're a good stop after walking the morning market.

faq.q: How much does breakfast cost in Rayong?
faq.a: Single-plate savory dishes like noodles, congee and pork blood soup mostly run about ฿40–70. Dim sum is ฿20–25 per basket, so even ordering several stays affordable. Coffee at the old-town cafes runs about ฿60–120 depending on what you get.
